events.reason: Suprapubic pain and gross hematuria after motor vehicle collision

documents.title: ED and Brief Hospital Summary (outside)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Outside hospital. Admit 6/22/2024, discharge 6/24/2024.
25M, high-speed MVC. Third crash-related visit in 2.5 years per records. Severe suprapubic pain, gross hematuria.
PMH: ADHD, tobacco use, alcohol use disorder, R femoral head AVN, prior C6 fracture. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.
ED: hemodynamically stable, in distress from pain. Abdomen soft, suprapubic tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Pelvic XR: R pubic rami fracture. FAST negative for free fluid. Foley placed - gross hematuria.
CT cystogram: extraperitoneal bladder rupture. No intraperitoneal extravasation.
Urology: nonoperative, catheter drainage ~2 weeks, cystogram before removal.
Ortho: pelvic fracture nonoperative, WBAT.
Course uneventful. Discharged home with indwelling Foley and leg bag. Urology f/u for cystogram in 2 weeks.

documents.title: hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: another accident saturday. broke my pelvis on the right and tore my bladder. home yesterday with a catheter for 2 weeks. do i need to see you

documents.title: RE: hospital again
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry to hear this, Rowan. Yes - we booked you Monday 7/1 at 10:40. If you get fever, the catheter stops draining, or belly pain gets worse, go to the ED. We've asked the hospital for records.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up: pelvic fracture, bladder injury

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25M seen after 6/22-6/24 stay. Records received: R pubic rami fracture (nonop), extraperitoneal bladder rupture on CT cystogram, Foley for ~2 wks.
He says he'd had 'some beers' earlier that evening; won't say more.
Now: walking with a cane, pelvic pain improving. Foley draining clear yellow urine. No fever.
Exam: afebrile. Abd soft, mild suprapubic tenderness. Foley in place, urine clear. Walks with cane.
A/P:
1. Extraperitoneal bladder rupture - catheter care reviewed. Urology cystogram 7/8.
2. R pubic rami fracture - WBAT per ortho.
3. Alcohol use disorder / recurrent crashes - third serious crash. Long talk. Offered addiction medicine referral again; declined. He's open to 'thinking about it' - will raise at next visit.
4. ADHD - continue Adderall 20 BID.
Off work until urology and ortho clear.

documents.title: Urology Clinic Note (outside)
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Urology, 7/8/2024. Two weeks after extraperitoneal bladder rupture managed with catheter drainage. Cystogram today: no contrast extravasation, bladder healed. Foley removed in clinic; voided without difficulty before leaving. Return as needed.

documents.title: No-show follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt re: missed physical 8/26. Says he forgot, first week back at work. Rebooked 9/16 8:20 am.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25M annual (rescheduled from no-show).
Interval: MVC 6/22 - R pubic rami fracture and extraperitoneal bladder rupture; catheter out 7/8 after healed cystogram. Back to full duty late August.
Voiding normally, no blood in urine. No pelvic pain now.
Meds: Adderall 20 BID, cetirizine prn, albuterol prn.
Alcohol: AUDIT-C 6. Tobacco ~half ppd, 7 yrs.
Exam: well. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. R hip and pelvis nontender, full ROM, normal gait. Neuro normal.
UA today to check after bladder injury.
A/P:
- CMP, UA.
- Alcohol: addiction medicine referral offered a fourth time; he declines but says he isn't drinking before driving 'anymore.' Documented.
- Tobacco: declines help.
- Flu shot next month. COVID updated dose offered, declined.
- ADHD: continue.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rowan, your urine test is clean - no blood, so the bladder looks fully healed. Kidney and liver tests normal too.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Trivalent flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. No contraindications. 15 min wait, fine.

documents.title: Orthopedic Note (outside)
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body: Ortho, 3/27/2025. R femoral head AVN, surveillance. Asymptomatic. Radiographs R hip: no collapse, sphericity preserved, no arthritic change. Continue observation. Return for groin pain or in 2 years.

events.reason: Severe head trauma in motor vehicle collision

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Admission 6/22/2025 - 7/2/2025, neurocritical care. Received by fax 8/12/2025.
26M, unrestrained driver, car versus tree. Found unresponsive; intubated for airway protection.
PMH: ADHD, tobacco and alcohol use disorders, R femoral head AVN, prior C6 fracture, prior extraperitoneal bladder rupture. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.
Exam on arrival: pupils equal and reactive; no purposeful response to painful stimulus.
CT head without contrast: no skull fracture, no large focal hematoma; multiple small punctate hemorrhages at the gray-white matter junction and in deep brain structures.
Hospital course: remained comatose for more than 48 hours despite normalized vital signs; repeat CT without new findings. Findings consistent with diffuse axonal injury. Began following commands on hospital day 6, extubated day 7. Stimulant held during the stay.
Discharge diagnosis: diffuse axonal injury.
Disposition: to acute inpatient rehabilitation.

documents.title: Call from mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called (pt listed her as contact). Rowan was in another car accident Saturday night, in ICU, on a breathing machine, has a brain injury. She wanted us to know. Offered support; asked that the hospital send records when he's discharged. Message to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aware. Will follow up with family after discharge. Hold stimulant refills until we see him.

events.reason: Inpatient rehabilitation after diffuse axonal injury

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Acute rehab 7/2/2025 - 7/23/2025, after diffuse axonal injury from MVC 6/22.
Program: daily PT, OT and speech therapy.
At discharge: ambulating independently, independent in self-care, oriented, following multistep commands. Neurologic exam without focal deficit.
Medications at discharge: amphetamine-dextroamphetamine 20 mg twice daily resumed, cetirizine as needed, albuterol as needed.
Discharged home with mother. Outpatient therapy and neurology follow-up arranged.

documents.title: Phone note
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mother called, Rowan home from rehab yesterday, staying with her. Booked hospital follow-up 7/29 2:00 pm. Discharge papers to be brought in; summaries not yet received - request re-sent to both facilities.

events.reason: Follow-up after hospitalization and rehabilitation for brain injury

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M with his mother. Car vs tree 6/22, ICU then rehab, home 7/23. Hospital summaries not yet received; history from pt, mother and the discharge papers they brought: diffuse axonal injury, coma for a couple of days, off the ventilator after about a week, three weeks rehab.
He doesn't remember the crash or most of the ICU. Walking on his own. Staying at his mother's.
Meds per discharge papers: Adderall 20 BID (rehab restarted it), cetirizine prn, albuterol prn. Reconciled.
Exam: alert, oriented x3, conversant. Pupils equal, reactive. EOM full. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 all four limbs. Sensation intact. Finger-nose normal. Gait normal, tandem ok.
A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury - neuro exam nonfocal today. Outpatient therapy and neurology follow-up already set by rehab.
2. ADHD - continue Adderall 20 BID as restarted.
3. Alcohol use disorder - four crashes now. Discussed with him and his mother present, with his OK. He says he hasn't had a drink since the accident. Addiction medicine referral offered; he wants to wait.
4. Tobacco - not ready.
No work for now; follow neurology guidance. RTC after neurology visit or sooner.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M annual.
Interval: DAI 6/2025 after MVC; ICU 6/22-7/2, rehab to 7/23. Summaries now received (8/12) and reviewed. Outpatient therapy ongoing. Neurology visit October.
Back living in his apartment. Hasn't returned to work yet.
Alcohol: AUDIT-C 5; started having beer again on weekends 'a few.' Smoking half pack.
PHQ-9 4.
Meds: Adderall 20 BID, cetirizine prn, albuterol prn.
Exam: well. Oriented, fluent. CN intact. Strength and gait normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abd soft. Hip full ROM.
A/P:
- CMP, CBC, lipids.
- Alcohol after brain injury: told him alcohol is especially risky now. Declines referral.
- Tobacco: declines.
- Flu shot October. COVID updated dose - declined.
- ADHD: continue.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Note (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Neurology clinic 10/16/2025. Follow-up of diffuse axonal injury (6/2025). Completing outpatient therapy. Exam: alert, oriented, language normal, cranial nerves intact, strength, sensation, coordination and gait normal. No focal deficits. Plan: finish outpatient therapy as arranged; avoid alcohol; return in 6 months or as needed.

documents.title: Flu shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Questionnaire reviewed, no contraindications. No reaction after 15 minutes.
